summary: Iteration 38 — Absentees Month view 'Compare to last month' ribbon. Backend: 11/11 new pytest in test_iter38_absentees_comparison.py + 48/48 prior regression (iter37+iter36+iter35). Tests cover comparison key presence on month, absence on day/week (regression guard), per-row prev_/delta_ field shape & types, exact delta math (delta_absent_days, delta_total_absences, delta_attendance_percentage rounded to 1dp), null handling when prev_total_days=0, empty-month (year 2000 + 2099) ships zero-comparison block with correct prev_month string, class/section filter applied consistently to both months, RBAC (accounts sees comparison, parent gets 403). Frontend: confirmed via Playwright on /school/attendance — month mode shows absentees-compare-ribbon with compare-ribbon-headline 'Sliding — 26 more absences than last month', compare-ribbon-prev-label 'vs April 2026', three CompareTiles (Students 8/from1/+7, Absent 11/from0/+11, Sick 16/from1/+15) in red tone (worse), 8 absentee-delta-* chips with ▲ +N and attendance % delta. Day & Week modes correctly hide both the ribbon and the 'vs last month' column.
critical_code_review_comments: teacher_attendance.py list_absentees: prev-month aggregation runs only_absentees=False and pulls EVERY student with any attendance record in the prior month, which is intentional (so delta is correct for students absent last month / present this month). On schools with thousands of students this could be a heavy in-memory list. Consider $project-only-needed-fields or a $match restricting to absentees + students currently in `rows` (since rows is what's surfaced anyway, a student missing from prev_by_id implicitly gets prev_*=0). The current code already uses .get(sid, {}) with zero defaults, so restricting prev aggregation to {student_id: {$in: absentee_ids}} would be a strict optimisation with no behavioural change.

_empty_comparison() handles the case where current month has 0 absentees, but it does NOT consult the prior month — so if current=0 and prior=10, the response shows delta=0 instead of the correct -10 ('improving'). This contradicts the agent_to_agent_context_note that explicitly called out 'month with NO absentees in current but absentees in prior (delta should be negative — improving)'. Recommend: in the early-return branch (rows empty), still run the prev-month aggregation and emit real deltas (negative numbers) rather than zeros. Reproduction: pick a month where the school has no current absentees but had some in the prior month — observed deltas are all 0 from _empty_comparison() instead of negative. NOTE: in the demo seed today's empty-month case (year 2000) also has no prior data so this bug isn't surfaced by the current tests; documenting as a logic gap.

CompareTile reverseColor semantics: all three tiles set reverseColor=true meaning delta<0 -> green. For the 'Students with absences' tile this happens to be desirable, but conceptually 'more students with absences' isn't strictly the inverse of attendance health (a tile labelled 'students' usually colours up=green). Confirm with product owner; current behaviour is internally consistent (fewer = green) so I won't flag as a bug, just a UX consideration.
